solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Thread or line attached to card

parts.note: an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A sewing kit: thread or a line of yarn fixed to a piece of card.
explanation.definitionFit: To lace shoes or a corset is to pass a cord through the holes, which is threading it.

clue.text: See board game about new monster's home

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see

indicators.note: the board game is placed about, i.e. around, the abbreviation for new

parts.note: chess is played on a board

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and look at a board game about a newly invented monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places the abbreviation for new within the board game.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish lake is the legendary dwelling place of the creature nicknamed Nessie.

clue.text: Conservative member to reach a higher position

parts.note: C abbreviates Conservative, the UK political party
a limb, such as an arm or leg, is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A Tory MP striving to rise up the political ladder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member' looks like a member of parliament, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend or go up in status is a synonym for rising to a loftier rank.

clue.text: Meatiest stews producing round figure?

indicators.note: to stew is to mix and cook, so the letters of the clue word are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A cook claiming the stews with the most meat in them yield a plump figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stews' looks like a noun, the dishes, but works as a verb for the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough calculation gives a rounded number, a figure that is approximate rather than exact.

clue.text: Place a foot, part of it, on sand, agitating series of scrap dealers

parts.note: to step is to put a foot down
a toe is part of a foot

indicators.note: agitating means stirring up, so the letters of the two clue words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stepping onto sand and stirring it up with their toes.
explanation.walkthrough: STEPTOE AND SON was a British TV sitcom (1962-74) about a father and son running a rag-and-bone business, scavenging and selling junk.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitcom series followed two rag-and-bone men, traders in junk and second-hand goods.

clue.text: Layabout almost direly wasted

indicators.note: wasted means wrecked, signalling that the remaining letters are rearranged
almost means not quite all, so the clue word loses its final letter

explanation.surface: A lazy person is described as being terribly wasted, nearly ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last letter of DIRELY to leave DIREL, which 'wasted' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy person who does little work is a synonym for a loafer or slacker.

clue.text: Georgian city in the place of Los Angeles welcomes worker, say

parts.note: at means in the place, as in 'at home'

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the city abbreviation holds the insect

parts.note: a worker ant is an example of a worker

explanation.surface: A US city stands in for Los Angeles, taking in some labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Georgian' means of the US state of Georgia, not the country or the 18th-century period; 'welcomes' puts the insect inside the city abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: The state capital of Georgia in the USA is the largest city in that state.

clue.text: Treat with acid and the rest before hospital

indicators.note: before puts the first piece ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and the rest
H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Someone in a hospital being treated with acid and other remedies.
explanation.definitionFit: Engravers bite a design into metal using a corrosive, which is what this process means.

clue.text: Some of whatever Balzac's expressed in words

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Part of whatever the French novelist Balzac wrote is put into language.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken or written in language, rather than shown by gesture, is the oral or linguistic sense.

clue.text: More than a billion people found in machine search

indicators.note: found in says the answer lies within the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A huge number of people turn up in a search run by computer.
explanation.definitionFit: The population of China exceeds 1.4 billion, so its nationals number more than a thousand million.

clue.text: Flower I call "exotic"

indicators.note: exotic means strange or foreign, signalling that the letters are rearranged into an unusual form

explanation.surface: A gardener says they think a certain bloom is foreign-looking.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub bears fragrant purple or white blossoms, so it is a kind of bloom.

clue.text: Arrest old boy, one in powerful position

parts.note: to nab is to catch or arrest
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil of a school

explanation.surface: Police arresting a former pupil who now holds a lot of power.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a Mughal governor in India, the word now means a wealthy, influential person.

clue.text: Despot's extremely timely tirade

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the end letters of the following word are used

parts.note: a rant is a long angry speech, a tirade

explanation.surface: A dictator delivers an angry speech at just the right moment.
explanation.definitionFit: An absolute ruler who governs cruelly is a synonym for a dictator.

clue.text: I agree the woman has caught a flightless bird

indicators.note: to have caught something is to hold it inside, so the pronoun encloses the other pieces

parts.note: her refers to a woman
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that a woman has captured an ostrich-like bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has caught' puts ARHEA inside HER after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the cry of assent heard in Parliament, a spoken expression of approval.

clue.text: Mistaking one end of mastoid for the other, accept responsibility for flat bone

parts.note: to shoulder a burden is to accept it

indicators.text: Mistaking one end of mastoid for the other
indicators.note: mastoid begins with M and ends with D, so one of its end letters is swapped for the opposite end

parts.note: blame is responsibility for a fault

explanation.surface: A doctor confuses the ends of a mastoid bone, then owns up to the error.
explanation.walkthrough: The mastoid is a bone behind the ear, a tempting false lead. The M in BLAME becomes D.
explanation.definitionFit: The scapula is a broad, flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder.

clue.text: Hope abandoned with trouble over tragic role

indicators.note: abandoned means wild or unrestrained, signalling that the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone gives up hope with problems piling up over a tragic part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges HOPE, and 'over' reads the synonym for trouble upwards in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's beloved, who goes mad and drowns, is a famous part in a Shakespeare tragedy.

clue.text: Head striker's spread

definitions.meaning: a goat or ram that hits with its head is one that butts
a dairy product spread on bread

explanation.surface: A footballer who scores headers has a spread in the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that rams with its head is a butter; the dairy fat is spread on toast.

clue.text: Wicket struck, gutted eleven go pale

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for wicket
hit means struck

indicators.note: gutted means with the insides removed, so only the outer letters of the following word stay

explanation.surface: A cricket team, devastated after a wicket falls, turns white with shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' looks like British slang for very disappointed, but here it empties ELEVEN to EN.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose colour or blanch is to become whiter in the face.

clue.text: Large skin blemish shows up in thorough search

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the pieces read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes
a wart is a small growth on the skin

explanation.surface: A careful examination reveals a big wart on someone's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishing with a dragnet gives the sense of a sweeping search through a mass of material.

clue.text: Maybe a potato bin, I'm not sure

parts.note: a tub is a container like a bin
er is the sound of hesitation or uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly wondering if a bin might hold potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A swollen underground stem storing food; the potato is the best-known example.

clue.text: Swim and play cricket with the man

parts.note: to bat is to play cricket as a batsman
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man goes swimming and then plays a game of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a dip in the sea or a lake is a synonym for a swim.

clue.text: Are accessories to answer wager?

parts.note: a bet is a wager

explanation.surface: A question of whether certain fashion items match a gamble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accessories' suggests fashion items, but here means helpers in a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: An accessory to a crime aids it, so to help a criminal is to be an accomplice.

clue.text: Light wood, a thick piece turned over

indicators.note: turned over means the pieces are flipped round and read backwards

parts.note: a slab is a thick flat piece

explanation.surface: A thick lump of lightweight timber is flipped over.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical tree yields a very lightweight timber used for model aircraft.

clue.text: Seeing first couple last, admire ghost

indicators.note: first couple last says the opening two letters are moved to the end

parts.note: to respect is to admire

explanation.surface: On seeing the first pair of lovers last, someone admires a phantom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first couple last' moves RE to the end of RESPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spirit or apparition is a synonym for a phantom.

clue.text: Asian country had Latin converts

indicators.note: converts means changes into another form, signalling that the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An Asian nation once had people converting to Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: The kingdom formerly called Siam lies in Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Mock professional clown dropping stone

indicators.note: dropping means letting fall, so the abbreviation is removed from the clown

parts.note: a jester was a professional fool at court
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the unit of weight

explanation.surface: People taunt a paid clown who drops a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British unit of weight, 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride or scoff at someone is a synonym for taunting them.
